newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds soar on tame inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds soar on tame inflation data.

text.p: Stocks soared and long-term interest rates tumbled Tuesday after a pair of economic reports soothed investor jitters about inflation.

The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 179.01 points -- its second biggest one-day point gain -- to close at 6,962.03. Last Tuesday, the 30-share Dow soared 173 points, which also fell just shy of the record one-day gain of 187 points two days after the "Black Monday" crash of Oct. 19, 1987.

Bond prices also rallied. But the dollar fell against the German mark after the surprisingly weak reports on manufacturing and compensation lessened chances the Federal Reserve would raise short-term rates again soon, investors said.
Oil prices moved higher. Gold ended little changed.

The stock rally started after the government said that a key gauge of wage and benefit costs rose 0.6 percent in the first quarter, off from 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter and below forecasts for a 0.9 percent rise.
A separate report said orders for long-lasting durable goods fell 3 percent in March, the biggest monthly decline since a 3.6 percent fall last August.
The reports calmed fears the Fed might raise rates again soon. The central bank's policy-makers raised rates a quarter point on March 25 and meet again on May 20.
"Many people feel the probability of the Fed tighting has been reduced," said Douglas Cliggott, stock strategist at J.P. Morgan. "Our view is it's a bit premature to move in that direction."
The reports helped whet buyers' appetite for stocks after recent strong corporate earnings reports.
"You've got both portions of the equation working for you today," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management.
The buying frenzy was evident in the breadth of the rally as 2,091 stocks rose while 527 fell on heavy volume of 547 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 25.60 points, or 2.1 percent, to 1,242.63. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks jumped 21.09 points, or 2.7 percent, to 794.05.

The rally was just as explosive in the inflation-sensitive bond market, where the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury jumped 1-17/32, lowering its yield to 6.98 percent from Monday's 7.11 percent. The last time the yield closed below 7 percent was on March 26, when it also settled at 6.98 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
After the Fed raised rates in March, stocks began a month-long drop that shaved nearly 10 percent from the Dow.
The market's next economic data hurdle comes Wednesday morning with a report on first quarter gross domestic product, the broadest measure of the nation's economy.
In currency markets, the dollar fell to 1.7262 marks in late New York trading from 1.7325 late on Monday. It ended little changed against the Japanese yen, at 126.93 compared to 126.86.
"People have been trading (on) the interest rate differentials for quite a while now, and today would be a sell day," said Russell LaScala, chief dealer at Citibank.
Steady or lower rates would make the dollar less attractive.
Elsewhere, crude oil for June delivery rose 53 cents to $20.44 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Coffee prices jumped after Folgers Coffee raised its retail prices, signalling more worries about this year's supplies.
Coffee for May delivery rose 6.15 cents to 226.40 cents a pound at the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange in New York.
May gold rose 20 cents to $340.40 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index rose 43.5 points to 4,433.2. Tokyo's stock market was closed for a holiday and will reopen on Wednesday.
